article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Sunset Sherbert × Purple Punch
Breeder: Clearwater Genetics
THC Content: 23-26%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Tropical fruit, berry, grape, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to good
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Easy to intermediate

Mai Thai is one of those cannabis strains whose tropical name happens to fit the flower remarkably well, even though its genetics have nothing to do with traditional Thai marijuana. Clearwater Genetics created the modern version by crossing Sunset Sherbert with Purple Punch, pairing two intensely aromatic California hybrids with complementary strengths. Sherbert brings creamy fruit, berries, gas, and Cookies-family richness, while Purple Punch pushes the profile toward grape candy, vanilla, ripe fruit, dense resin, and deep purple coloration. The result became especially influential through the Mai Tai #4 selection, a plant Clearwater has repeatedly used as breeding material in later hybrids. Green Dot Labs has also maintained the same Sunset Sherbert × Purple Punch combination in its genetics library under the spelling “Mai Thai,” describing the palate simply and appropriately as a sweet, fruity cocktail.

The cultivar is appealing because neither parent completely overwhelms the other. Properly grown flower can smell like berries, grape, citrus peel, tropical fruit, cream, and vanilla before a modest layer of earthy gas appears underneath. Dense flowers frequently take on lavender or purple tones beneath a heavy trichome coating, giving the buds as much visual appeal as aromatic intensity. The high follows a similarly gradual transition: mood and sensory perception lift first, then a warmer physical calm begins replacing the initial cerebral brightness. That balance has helped Mai Thai remain useful not only as finished weed but as a breeding parent behind numerous Clearwater projects.
Genetics and Lineage

The verified direct lineage is Sunset Sherbert × Purple Punch. Clearwater Genetics currently lists Mai Tai with precisely that parentage, and Green Dot Labs independently identifies its Mai Thai selection with the same cross. This is important because an older, unrelated strain carrying the Mai Tai name has circulated with Maui Wowie and Tutti Frutti genetics. The Clearwater version covered here is the modern Sunset Sherbert × Purple Punch cultivar and should not be combined with that separate family tree.

Sunset Sherbert contributes a major Cookies-family branch to the pedigree. The cultivar descends from GSC crossed with Pink Panties and is associated with sweet berry, grape, cream, citrus, and gas. Purple Punch brings a second heavily fruit-oriented lineage through Granddaddy Purple and Larry OG . Its best-known characteristics include grape candy, berry, vanilla, compact floral structure, heavy trichome production, and a calmer physical effect. Those parents overlap in sweetness but differ enough underneath to give Mai Thai substantially more dimension than a simple fruit strain.

Clearwater’s Mai Tai #4 became especially valuable as a breeder because it reliably transmits color, resin, fruit character, and structure into offspring. The cut appears behind Clearwater hybrids such as Astronaut Status, Mint Smash, Bittersweet, and numerous limited crosses. That continued use says something important about the plant: elite cannabis breeders rarely keep returning to a parent unless it contributes traits consistently enough to justify the space it occupies in a breeding program.
Effects and Experience

The opening effects tend to arrive with an easygoing cerebral lift rather than a jarring rush. Mood may brighten, music becomes more engaging, conversation feels easier, and food or visual entertainment can become unusually interesting. The mental side is generally euphoric and comfortable rather than aggressively stimulating, making moderate amounts well suited to relaxed social settings, movies, gaming, music, or an afternoon with few demanding obligations.

Physical relaxation begins filling in underneath that brighter first stage as the experience matures. Shoulders may loosen, activity can feel less urgent, and the high gradually becomes more immersive. That transition reflects the character of both parents: Sunset Sherbert provides a smooth, mentally enjoyable beginning, while Purple Punch contributes greater body weight. A moderate serving can remain pleasantly balanced, whereas a larger amount may become distinctly heavier and more appropriate for evening use.

Although one fixed THC percentage cannot accurately describe every harvest, Mai Thai should generally be treated as high-potency marijuana. Individual commercial examples and selections regularly fall in the 20% range, and the sensory smoothness of the cultivar can make it easy to underestimate the dose. Excessive THC may cause impaired short-term memory, dizziness, anxiety, dry mouth, slowed reaction time, or pronounced lethargy. Consumers with limited tolerance should approach unfamiliar batches conservatively.
Medical Benefits

Mai Thai has not undergone clinical testing as a treatment for a specific medical condition. Its relaxing and mood-elevating reputation may interest some medical cannabis patients seeking temporary relief from discomfort, stress, low appetite, or difficulty winding down, but a cultivar name does not guarantee a particular therapeutic response. Chemistry can change substantially between growers, harvests, and individual phenotypes.

Research involving cannabis and cannabinoids more broadly suggests modest benefit for some forms of chronic pain and certain symptom-related sleep problems, but those results cannot be automatically transferred to this strain. Many studies also involve cannabinoid preparations that differ significantly from inhaled high-THC flower. The evidence is therefore more useful for understanding cannabis generally than for claiming that Mai Thai treats pain, insomnia, anxiety, or another disorder.

Potential drawbacks are equally relevant. THC may worsen anxiety in sensitive individuals and can impair concentration, judgment, memory, and coordination. Cannabinoids may also interact with some prescription medications. People using marijuana for persistent symptoms or alongside other medications should discuss cannabinoid use with an appropriate healthcare professional rather than relying solely on strain reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Mai Thai’s aroma earns the cocktail comparison without needing artificial flavoring or a literal tropical parent. Green Dot Labs summarizes the profile as a sweet and fruity cocktail, while flower from the Mai Tai #4 line commonly expands that description into ripe berry, grape, sugared citrus, cream, vanilla, and softer floral notes. Breaking apart the buds can bring out a slightly deeper earthy or gassy layer that keeps the perfume from becoming excessively sugary.

The flavor usually develops in stages. Sweet fruit and grape may appear first, followed by citrus and creamy dessert notes through the middle of the inhale. Vanilla, berry skin, floral sweetness, and faint gas can linger afterward. That combination reflects the parents unusually well: Purple Punch contributes the darker grape-and-vanilla side, while Sunset Sherbert supplies citrus, berry, cream, and fuel.

A documented Mai Tai #4 selection grown by Jubel Exotics lists myrcene, limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool among its terpene profile. Those compounds fit the sensory picture: limonene supports the citrus brightness, myrcene can reinforce fruit and earthy depth, beta-caryophyllene contributes spice, and linalool can add softer floral character. The profile belongs to a selected cultivation rather than every plant bearing the name, so exact terpene percentages should always be taken from the specific batch being consumed.
Growing Information

Mai Tai #4 has developed a reputation among growers for being considerably more manageable than some exotic California hybrids. The Purple Punch side contributes a cooperative, sturdy frame, while Sunset Sherbert adds strong resin production and colorful flowers. The plant can develop attractive purple and lavender pigmentation during bloom, particularly when genetics and environmental conditions favor anthocyanin expression. Growers should view color as a genetic and environmental characteristic rather than a maturity indicator.

Jubel Exotics lists a nine-week flowering period for its verified Clearwater Mai Tai #4 cut. That approximately 63-day schedule provides the most useful documented flowering reference for the recognized selection, although individual seed phenotypes may finish somewhat earlier or later. Clearwater itself does not currently publish an official universal outdoor harvest date or numerical yield specification for the cultivar.

Structurally, the plant can respond well to canopy management. Topping or low-stress training where cultivation is legal can spread growth across multiple branches and improve light exposure, particularly before the flowering stretch begins. Dense resinous flowers require reliable airflow later in bloom, since trapped humidity around compact buds can increase the risk of quality problems. Branch support may become useful on heavier phenotypes as the flowers gain mass.

Post-harvest conditions are particularly important because the cultivar’s appeal depends so strongly on volatile fruit and floral compounds. Drying too quickly or at excessive temperatures can flatten the citrus and tropical notes, leaving behind a more ordinary earthy sweetness. A controlled dry followed by a gradual cure helps preserve berry, vanilla, grape, and creamy aromatics while allowing moisture inside the flower to equalize. Growers chasing bag appeal should remember that colorful flowers and heavy trichomes matter far less if the curing process strips away the qualities that made Mai Thai desirable in the first place.
FAQ
What strain is Mai Thai?

Mai Thai, more commonly spelled Mai Tai by its breeder, is a Clearwater Genetics hybrid made from Sunset Sherbert × Purple Punch. Green Dot Labs also carries a Mai Thai selection with the same lineage.
Who bred Mai Thai?

Clearwater Genetics is the breeder associated with the modern Sunset Sherbert × Purple Punch Mai Tai and the influential Mai Tai #4 selection. Clearwater has used Mai Tai #4 extensively as a parent in later breeding projects.
Is Mai Thai the same as Maui Wowie × Tutti Frutti?

No. An older cultivar carrying the Mai Tai name has been described with Maui Wowie × Tutti Frutti genetics, creating substantial confusion. The Clearwater Genetics version covered here is Sunset Sherbert × Purple Punch.
What does Mai Thai taste like?

Expect sweet berry, grape, tropical fruit, citrus, cream, vanilla, and floral notes with a modest earthy-gas finish. Green Dot Labs characterizes its same-lineage Mai Thai selection as having a sweet, fruity cocktail palate.
How long does Mai Thai take to flower?

A verified Clearwater Mai Tai #4 clone maintained by Jubel Exotics is listed at approximately nine weeks of flowering. Seed-grown plants may vary somewhat depending on phenotype and environmental conditions.
Final Thoughts on Mai Thai

Mai Thai has remained relevant because its genetics combine two highly complementary forms of modern California cannabis. Sunset Sherbert supplies creamy berries, citrus, sweetness, and gas, while Purple Punch contributes grape candy, vanilla, color, dense resin, and greater physical relaxation. Clearwater Genetics brought those parents together in a hybrid that became more influential through Mai Tai #4 than its tropical name alone would suggest.

Its value as breeding stock reinforces the quality of the original selection. Clearwater has repeatedly incorporated Mai Tai #4 into newer projects, including crosses that went on to establish reputations of their own. The plant’s ability to transmit resin, pigmentation, fruit-forward terpenes, and workable structure makes it more than a fashionable dispensary cultivar.

For consumers, the attraction is a flavorful progression from berry, grape, tropical citrus, and cream into a smooth relaxing high. For cultivators, approximately nine weeks of flowering, strong resin production, attractive coloration, and manageable architecture make the recognized #4 selection especially interesting. Most importantly, a reliable strain reference should keep the genetics straight: the modern Mai Thai/Mai Tai discussed here is Clearwater Genetics’ Sunset Sherbert × Purple Punch hybrid—not the unrelated Maui Wowie × Tutti Frutti cultivar that happens to share the cocktail-inspired name.
